newsitem.title: FRANCE: Parliament adopts amendments to ONP update directive.
newsitem.headline: Parliament adopts amendments to ONP update directive.

text.p: The European Parliament approved six amendments on Wednesday to a draft directive that would update EU rules on access to public telecommunications networks to take account of the 1998 liberalisation deadline.

It said the Commission should examine the possibility of creating a telecoms European Regulatory Authority and draw up a draft directive on financing universal service -- affordable basic phone service for all consumers -- before January 31, 1997.

The parliament was voting on the Council's common position on proposal COM(95)543, which would update the framework Open Network Provision (ONP) directive, 90/387/EEC, and a related directive applying specifically to leased lines, 92/44/EEC.
ONP directives set out rules to guarantee that customers or competitors have fair access to public telecoms networks.

Voting on a report by Belgian EPP deputy Fernand Herman, the parliament said two references in an annex to a harmonised approach to numbering should also mention "number portability" -- the ability of consumers to take their phone numbers with them when they change telecoms operators.
It also tightened up the definition of "leased lines" to cover "fixed public telephone network lines used exclusively for the voice telephony service".
